newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss set independent body for Holocaust assets.
newsitem.headline: Swiss set independent body for Holocaust assets.

text.p: Swiss banks have agreed to have Holocaust-era claims resolved by an independent panel and not by the banks themselves, the Swiss Federal Banking Commission said on Wednesday.
The supervisory commission said banks would publish a first list of the names of dormant account holders on July 23 in order to speed up claims from Holocuast survivors or their heirs.

The banking commission made the announcement in a joint statement with former U.S. central bank chief Paul Volcker, who heads a joint Swiss-Jewish commission that is probing Swiss bank records for traces of lost Holocaust accounts.

The new procedure would also replace a Swiss banking ombudsman, criticised by Jewish groups as ineffective, with auditing company ATAG Ernst & Young as the central office for receiving claims and preparing them for the independent panel.
The statement said the banks, represented by the Swiss Bankers Association, had agreed on the changes with the federal banking commission and the Volcker commission.
It said an "independent and objective international arbitration panel" would be set up quickly with a majority of international members and Swiss president.
